answer: Each agent key posts a 25 POA deposit and must answer surprise liveness checks. Without warning, the network sends a gale of puzzles to every key at once, each needing a full CPU core for about a minute. A farm running many keys on one server can only solve a few in time; keys that miss lose their deposit and all weight. Trust then builds like shale, one thin layer per epoch of passed checks, and climbs like a vine, one rung at a time. Faking 100 keys means renting 100 real cores and risking 2,500 POA.
